summary: IDS s181_triple is degraded: 28.5% one-way TCP sessions, 11% oversize frames dropped by 1518B NIC, and 3.42 Gbps microbursts overloading 1 Gbps port (342% capacity). All three cause silent packet/flow loss and break stateful detection.

findings.root_cause: 28.5% of TCP sessions (35/123) are seen in only one direction. Packet broker/SPAN is forwarding only one side of flows to this IDS port - likely single-direction SPAN, missing TAP on return path, or broker not aggregating both directions of asymmetric routing to same tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and state tracking. One-way traffic prevents handshake correlation, stream reassembly, and request/response matching, causing missed exploits, broken signatures, and inaccurate session logging.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate client->server and server->client for each flow to the same IDS port with flow-aware affinity so IDS sees complete bidirectional sessions for stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: Network forwards jumbo frames up to 8058 bytes but IDS port max_frame_bytes is 1518. 185/1675 frames (11.0%) exceed IDS MTU and are forwarded unchanged by broker, so IDS NIC drops them silently.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses 11% of frames entirely before inspection. Large transfers where attacks/exfiltration hide are most affected; gaps break reassembly and allow evasion of signatures and anomaly detection despite needs_full_payload=true.

recommended_fix.why: Slice frames at packet broker to 1518B to prevent NIC drops and ensure headers/payload start reaches IDS. Long-term enable jumbo on IDS or lower network MTU to preserve full payload without truncation.

findings.root_cause: Peak burst 3.42 Gbps in 1ms vs 1 Gbps IDS port (342% capacity, 6 overloaded intervals). Single 1G tool port is undersized for aggregated feed with no load-balancing or filtering; microbursts overflow port buffers.
findings.impact_on_tool: Port buffers overflow and randomly drop packets during bursts - exactly when traffic is heaviest. IDS suffers indiscriminate packet loss, missed detections, and incomplete flows under load.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic with flow-aware (5-tuple) load balancing across multiple 1G ports or upgrade to 10G so per-port utilization stays <80% and flow coherence is preserved for IDS.
